Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the ShopNova Inc. Q4 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. To ask a question, you will need to press star one on your telephone keypad. There will be an opportunity to ask a question after the presentation. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to ShopNova Inc.'s Q4 earnings call. Joining me today are Elena Vasquez, CEO; Marcus Hale, CFO; Jordan Lee, COO; Sophia Chen, CMO; Raj Patel, CTO; Lila Novak, CDO; and Theo Grant, CSO.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call may contain forward-looking statements, including our expectations for future financial performance, business strategies, and market trends. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete list of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Elena Vasquez, CEO of ShopNova Inc.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Alex, and good afternoon, everyone. We are pleased to report a strong Q4 performance, driven by robust gross merchandise value growth despite macroeconomic pressures, and significant expansion in our active customer base. We saw significant growth in key metrics, with GMV reaching $2.85 billion, up 15% year-over-year, fueled by holiday momentum and marketplace momentum.

Our focus remains on enhancing seller tools and platform monetization. We are also excited about the initial traction we are seeing with our ShopNova Prime loyalty program enhancements, which we believe will significantly boost repeat revenue and lifetime value.

We are investing heavily in supply chain resilience and fulfillment network expansion to counter disruptions.

We are focused on improving marketing efficiency and customer acquisition dynamics.

We are expanding our presence in high-growth regions like APAC and EMEA.

We are enhancing our customer experience through AI-powered personalization and seamless omnichannel options.

Finally, we are committed to sustainability initiatives that reduce our environmental footprint while appealing to conscious consumers.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Marcus Hale, our CFO, to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Marcus Hale:
Thank you, Elena. Our Q4 revenue was $565 million, an increase of 18% year-over-year. Gross margin was 42%, driven by take rate expansion to 19.8%, improved product mix toward higher-margin categories, and fulfillment efficiencies amid stabilizing freight costs. Operating expenses were $385 million, representing 68% of revenue. Marketing spend rose 18% year-over-year to $285 million, but delivered outsized returns through declining customer acquisition costs and superior ROAS.

Our net income for the quarter was $85 million, or $0.52 per share. We ended the quarter with $2.2 billion in cash and cash equivalents. We are reaffirming our full-year guidance of $6.0 to $6.3 billion in revenue and 14% adjusted EBITDA margins.

To provide more color on the drivers behind these results, let me turn first to our customer acquisition cost, or CAC, and the efficiency of our marketing spend—a vital element for sustainable scaling in this competitive online retail space. Optimizing CAC goes beyond cost reduction; it's about amplifying customer lifetime value while efficiently growing our active base. In Q4, we hit a blended CAC of $42, down 12.5% from $48 a year ago and better than $45 in Q3—this is our sixth consecutive quarter of declines, even with headwinds from high interest rates dampening discretionary spending and the phase-out of third-party cookies on major browsers.

Our $285 million in marketing investments, up 18% year-over-year, powered 6.8 million new customers, a 22% increase, at that efficient $42 CAC. This outperforms peers—Shopify cohorts average $55, while DTC brands like Warby Parker report $60-70 post-privacy changes. ROAS reached 4.8x, up from 4.2x, with payback in 5.2 months versus industry 8-10 months for apparel and electronics. Our LTV-to-CAC ratio is 6.2:1, with $260 trailing LTV, thanks to ShopNova Prime's 28 million members driving 65% of repeats.

Channel-wise, paid social at 42% of spend yielded $38 CAC and 5.1x ROAS via ML lookalikes on first-party data from 150 million transactions. Search and shopping ads at 35% spend hit $46 CAC but 6.2x ROAS with bid optimization. Emerging TikTok and Pinterest at 15% spend pulled CAC to $32 through viral drops.

Post-ATT and iOS impacts, our 40% ramp in zero- and first-party data via quizzes and surveys captures 72% of signals, offsetting 10% CPM rises to $18 on Meta and $4.50 on Google. Regionally, North America at 68% revenue held US CAC at $50 with Walmart integrations, Canada dropped 8% to $44, EMEA at $58 faced GDPR costs but SEO lifted organics, and APAC shone at $28 via influencers and Shopee storefronts.

Tech like our Snowflake-TensorFlow CDP with 1,200 micro-cohorts cut waste 22%, boosted conversions 15% to 4.2%. Server-side tracking recaptures 85% attribution, AI creatives lift CTRs 28%, and Trade Desk pilots show 18% gains.

Forward, retention-first acquisition via personalized recs (32% of orders) and CTV reallocation targets 5.5x ROAS. With 35% organic traffic, we aim for 28 million new customers at sub-$45 CAC, supporting 25% growth and 14% EBITDA.

Building on marketing momentum, let's discuss advertising and marketing spend efficiency through ROAS. ROAS—revenue per ad dollar—is our guidepost for profitable scaling amid inflation and sentiment softness. Q4 blended ROAS was 5.8x, up 16% quarter-over-quarter from 5.0x and 22% year-over-year from 4.8x, generating $1.47 billion incremental revenue from $253 million spend—12.1% of $2.09 billion GMV, down 80 bps as percent.

Beating eMarketer's 4.2x industry average, paid search led at 6.2x with high-intent keywords, Meta at 4.7x via DCO despite CPM hikes, TikTok/Pinterest at 7.1x on videos. Our RetailCo Media Network hit 8.4x for partners, 6.9x owned.

North America at 6.0x with same-day delivery, Europe to 5.3x localized, APAC 5.6x despite Red Sea issues. Vertex AI bid optimization lifted 21%, first-party data boosts match rates to 78%, incrementality tests refine attribution.

We've cut brand spend 15%, piloting AR on Snapchat for 9x ROAS. Q1 outlook: 6.1-6.3x ROAS.

Next, seller performance metrics underscore our marketplace strength. We ended Q4 with 2.8 million active sellers—those with $1,000+ trailing GMV—up 28% from 2.2 million. SMBs at 72% or 2 million grew 32% on zero-fee onboarding, enterprises to 45,000 up 18%.

North America 1.4 million up 25%, APAC 850,000 up 45% via Shopee ties, Europe 400,000 up 15%, emerging 150,000 up 60%. Annualized revenue per seller hit $48,200, up 14% from $42,300; median $22,500 up 11%, top 1% at $850,000.

Seller AI Suite lifts 17% for 65% adopters, 25 new FBO centers boost adoption to 42% GMV, category tools grow home & garden 25%. Quality thresholds cut churn to 8%. Outlook: 3.2 million sellers, $52,000 revenue per.

Seasonality shaped Q4, with 46% FY GMV share. Trends show Q4 3.5-4.2x Q2, but we hit 15% YoY on $2.85 billion GMV versus 25% guide. BFCM $1.12 billion up 12%, Cyber Monday 2.1 million orders at $89 AOV.

Deviations from macro—inflation crimped AOV conversions 4%, Red Sea delayed 15% inventory. North America +14% but -6% forecast, EMEA +22%, APAC +9%. NovaAI forecasting at 92% accuracy, Seasonal Surge Mode cuts delivery to 1.8 days, vendor models cut stockouts 40%.

Mitigations include subscriptions at 8% recurring, B2B pilots. FY25 GMV $7.2-7.5 billion, Q4 45%.

Macro factors weighed on results: Q4 GMV $2.85 billion up 15% but below guide, revenue $565 million up 18% on 19.8% take rate. Inflation at 3.2% squeezed AOV 15% in apparel, staples resilient. Pivoted to NovaValue private label capturing 22% orders.

Rates curbed big-ticket, BNPL to 18% but fees up 5%. Freight down 60% cut COGS 8%. North America +10%, Europe flat, APAC +18%. Trade-down to <$50 items, NovaPrime 55% GMV. MESI-integrated forecasting at 92% accuracy.

Logistics at 14.2% revenue or $285 million up 23% YoY from disruptions—Red Sea spiked rates 35%, air premiums $22 million, last-mile +17%, holding $18 million. Per order $8.74 from $7.12.

North America 15.8%, Europe 16.5%, APAC 11.2%. OmniRoute saves $15 million, AMRs cut labor 12%, MFCs 45% same-day, nearshoring. Q3 guide 13.5-14.0%.

Take rate 19.8% up 130 bps YoY from pricing (+70 bps: Prime tiers 22-25%, ads CPC $0.42), promos (+50 bps: waivers down 60%), mix (+10 bps: luxury 28% GMV). North America 20.5%, Europe 18.9%, APAC 18.2%. TakeRate Optimizer 92% elasticity. Q4 20.0-20.3%.

Finally, fulfillment cost per order at $8.47, down 8% YoY from $9.20. Automation with 1,200 AMRs cuts pick 35%, PeakPredict 28% efficiency, last-mile partnerships drop $3.67. North America $8.12, Europe $9.84, APAC $8.91. Target sub-$8 by 2025.

These dynamics affirm our path to profitable growth.

Now I'll turn it over to Jordan Lee to discuss operations.

Jordan Lee:
Thanks, Marcus. Operationally, we focused on network expansion and automation scaling. Our shipping times improved by 25% to 1.8 days average. Fulfillment costs improved 8% per order to $8.47. We are implementing AI route optimization across 45 centers.

Now I'll turn it over to Sophia Chen.

Sophia Chen:
Thanks, Jordan. From a marketing perspective, we saw strong results from paid social and retail media networks. Customer acquisition costs were $42. Our brand awareness increased by 18%. We are focusing on high-ROAS channels like TikTok Shop.

Now I'll turn it over to Raj Patel.

Raj Patel:
Thanks, Sophia. On the technology front, we've been focused on AI personalization and cookieless tracking. Our website uptime was 99.99%. Mobile app usage increased by 30%. We're investing in Vertex AI bid engines and CDP enhancements.

Now I'll turn it over to Lila Novak.

Lila Novak:
Thanks, Raj. Data science is a key focus for us. We've seen a 15% improvement in conversion rates because of micro-cohort segmentation. We are also focusing on privacy-safe attribution models.

Now I'll turn it over to Theo Grant.

Theo Grant:
Thanks, Lila. Sustainability is very important to us. We reduced our carbon footprint by 20%. We are committed to EV last-mile fleets and reusable packaging initiatives.

Operator, we are now ready for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, at this time we will open the floor for questions. [Operator instructions for Q&A session]. Our first question comes from Sarah Thompson with Goldman Sachs.

Sarah Thompson:
Thanks, and congrats on the quarter. Elena, given the macro pressures you called out, how are you thinking about FY25 GMV growth and any seasonality adjustments?

Elena Vasquez:
Thanks, Sarah. Solid question. As Marcus detailed, Q4 GMV grew 15% despite inflation squeezing AOV and supply delays—our MESI modeling and NovaAI captured those dynamics, flattening troughs via subscriptions now at 8% recurring. We're guiding 18-22% FY25 GMV to $7.2-7.5 billion, with Q4 still ~45%, but off-peak loyalty nudges targeting Q1 at 25% share.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Kim with Morgan Stanley.

David Kim:
Marcus, can you expand on take rate drivers and sustainability into next year?

Marcus Hale:
Absolutely, David. The 130 bps expansion to 19.8% came from Prime tier pricing, promo discipline reducing waivers 60%, and luxury mix. TakeRate Optimizer ensures low churn; we see 20.5% trailing by year-end, resilient to competition.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with JPMorgan.

Lisa Chen:
Jordan, on logistics—how are Red Sea impacts fading, and FCPO outlook?

Jordan Lee:
Great point, Lisa. Disruptions added $45 million last-mile, but OmniRoute and carrier diversification saved $15 million. FCPO $8.47 reflects 14% baseline cuts; Q1 $8.30-8.50 as rates normalize, targeting sub-12% long-term.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Rodriguez with Barclays.

Mike Rodriguez:
Sophia, impressive CAC—channel shifts and ROAS details?

Sophia Chen:
Thanks, Mike. Blended $42 CAC, 5.8x ROAS from social 5.1x, search 6.2x, TikTok 7.1x. First-party data and DCO offset CPMs; CTV pilots for 6x+ ahead.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Priya Singh with Deutsche Bank.

Priya Singh:
Raj, tech investments—how's CDP tying to seller tools?

Raj Patel:
Priya, spot on. Seller AI on 15PB data lifts revenue 17%, integrated with CDP for forecasts. Uptime 99.99%, app +30% via personalization driving 32% orders.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Tom Ellis with Citi.

Tom Ellis:
Lila, data privacy amid cookie loss—conversion impacts?

Lila Novak:
Tom, server-side and Sandbox recapture 85%, micro-cohorts +15% conversions to 4.2%. Zero-party data at 72% buffers us well.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emma Walsh with RBC Capital.

Emma Walsh:
Theo, sustainability—link to costs and seller metrics?

Theo Grant:
Emma, 20% footprint cut via 18% EV fleets saved $12 million credits. Ties to sellers: quality thresholds and green tools boost retention, aligning with APAC growth.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I would now like to turn the call back over to Elena Vasquez for closing remarks.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you for joining us today. We are confident in our ability to continue to execute our strategy and deliver long-term value for our shareholders. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
